units.title: How Screens Work
units.tip: Displays create images by controlling light. LCD screens use a backlight and liquid crystals to block or allow light through. OLED screens emit their own light from individual pixels.

exercises.question: What does LCD stand for?
exercises.answer: Liquid Crystal Display
exercises.explain: LCD is the technology behind most monitors and older phone screens. Liquid crystals twist to control how much light passes through.

exercises.question: How does an LCD screen produce light?
exercises.answer: A backlight shines through liquid crystals
exercises.explain: LCD screens have a bright light source behind them. Liquid crystal layers twist to block or pass light, creating the image you see.
choices: A backlight shines through liquid crystals
Magnets attract and repel light particles

exercises.question: What is a pixel?
exercises.answer: The smallest colored dot that makes up a display
exercises.explain: Pixels are tiny colored lights. Thousands or millions of pixels arranged in a grid create the image on your screen.
choices: The smallest colored dot that makes up a display

exercises.question: What are subpixels?
exercises.answer: Tiny red, green, or blue parts that make up each pixel
exercises.explain: Each pixel contains three subpixels: red, green, and blue. By mixing light from these three colors at different brightness levels, any color can be created.
choices: Tiny red, green, or blue parts that make up each pixel

exercises.question: Why do LCD screens need a backlight?
exercises.answer: Liquid crystals only block or pass light, they don't produce it
exercises.explain: Liquid crystals are like tiny shutters. They control light but don't create it, so a backlight behind them is essential.
choices: Liquid crystals only block or pass light, they don't produce it

exercises.question: What does OLED stand for?
exercises.answer: Organic Light-Emitting Diode
exercises.explain: OLED is a newer display technology where each pixel produces its own light instead of relying on a shared backlight.

exercises.question: How do OLED pixels produce light?
exercises.answer: Each pixel emits light when current flows through it
exercises.explain: OLED pixels are self-luminous. When electricity passes through the organic material, it glows. No backlight needed.
choices: Each pixel emits light when current flows through it

exercises.question: What happens when an OLED pixel turns off?
exercises.answer: No light is produced from that pixel
exercises.explain: In an OLED screen, off pixels produce zero light, creating true blacks. This saves power and improves contrast compared to LCD.
choices: No light is produced from that pixel

exercises.question: Why do OLED screens typically have better contrast than LCD?
exercises.answer: OLED pixels produce true black when off
exercises.explain: LCD screens always have some backlight coming through, so blacks are actually dark gray. OLED pixels can turn completely off, creating perfect black and infinite contrast.
choices: OLED pixels produce true black when off

exercises.question: What is a disadvantage of OLED displays?
exercises.answer: Pixels can wear out over time, causing burn-in
exercises.explain: OLED pixels gradually dim with use. If the same image stays on screen for weeks, those pixels may be permanently darker than the rest.
choices: They are less bright than LCD
Pixels can wear out over time, causing burn-in
They use more power than LCD

units.title: Resolution and Pixel Density
units.tip: Resolution is how many pixels fit on the screen, measured as width by height. Pixel density measures how closely packed pixels are, making the image sharper.

exercises.question: What does a resolution of 1920x1080 mean?
exercises.answer: 1920 pixels wide and 1080 pixels tall
exercises.explain: Resolution describes the grid size. 1920x1080 means the screen contains 1920 columns and 1080 rows of pixels.

exercises.question: Why do higher resolutions show more detail?
exercises.answer: More pixels means finer details can be drawn
exercises.explain: With more pixels, images can contain finer details and smoother curves. Each pixel is smaller, so the image looks sharper.
choices: More pixels means finer details can be drawn

exercises.question: What is 4K resolution?
exercises.answer: Approximately 4000 pixels wide, around 3840x2160
exercises.explain: 4K is an ultra-high resolution with roughly four times the pixels of 1080p. It provides extremely sharp images for detailed work.

exercises.question: Can two screens have the same resolution but look different?
exercises.answer: Yes, if they are different sizes the pixel density differs
exercises.explain: A 1080p 24-inch monitor and a 1080p 32-inch monitor have the same resolution but different pixel densities. The larger screen looks less sharp.
choices: Only if one uses LCD and one uses OLED
Yes, if they are different sizes the pixel density differs
Only if the colors are different
No, resolution determines how things look

exercises.question: What does 'native resolution' mean?
exercises.answer: The number of pixels the screen physically has
exercises.explain: Native resolution is the actual pixel count. Scaling images to a different resolution can look blurry or stretched.
choices: A standard set by the government
The number of pixels the screen physically has

exercises.question: What is pixel density measured in?
exercises.answer: Pixels per inch (PPI) or dots per inch (DPI)
exercises.explain: Pixel density tells you how many pixels fit in one inch of screen. Higher density means sharper images because pixels are smaller.
choices: Pixels per inch (PPI) or dots per inch (DPI)

exercises.question: What happens to image sharpness when pixel size increases?
exercises.answer: The image becomes pixelated and less sharp
exercises.explain: Larger pixels are more visible, making the image look blocky. You can see individual dots instead of smooth lines and curves.
choices: The image becomes pixelated and less sharp

exercises.question: Why do phone screens typically have higher pixel density than monitor screens?
exercises.answer: Phones are held closer to your eyes, so pixels are more visible
exercises.explain: Your phone is a few inches from your eyes, while a monitor is farther away. Pixels are more noticeable at close distances, so phones need higher density to look sharp.
choices: Phones are held closer to your eyes, so pixels are more visible

exercises.question: What does 'retina display' mean?
exercises.answer: Pixel density high enough that individual pixels are not visible
exercises.explain: A retina display has enough pixels per inch that, from normal viewing distance, the human eye cannot see individual pixels. The image looks smooth and continuous.
choices: A display that uses LED technology
A display with red, green, and blue pixels
Pixel density high enough that individual pixels are not visible
A display that reduces eye strain

exercises.question: How does viewing distance affect perceived sharpness?
exercises.answer: Closer viewing distances require higher pixel density for sharpness
exercises.explain: When you hold a device close, individual pixels become visible at lower densities. Farther viewing distances forgive lower pixel density.
choices: Viewing distance does not affect sharpness
Closer viewing distances require higher pixel density for sharpness
Pixel density changes with viewing distance
Farther distances require higher pixel density

units.title: Color and Bit Depth
units.tip: Colors on screens are made by mixing red, green, and blue light at different brightness levels. Bit depth determines how many colors can be displayed.

exercises.question: What does RGB stand for?
exercises.answer: Red, Green, Blue
exercises.explain: RGB is the color model used by all screens. By controlling the intensity of red, green, and blue light in each pixel, any color can be created.

exercises.question: How many values can each color channel have in 8-bit color?
exercises.answer: 256 values, from 0 to 255
exercises.explain: 8 bits per channel means 2 to the power of 8 = 256 possible brightness levels for each color, from off (0) to full brightness (255).

exercises.question: What color does pure red look like in RGB?
exercises.answer: Red at 255, Green at 0, Blue at 0
exercises.explain: To show pure red, the red channel is at maximum (255) while green and blue are off (0). Mixing equal amounts of all three colors makes white.
choices: Red at 0, Green at 0, Blue at 255
Red at 200, Green at 55, Blue at 55
Red at 128, Green at 128, Blue at 128
Red at 255, Green at 0, Blue at 0

exercises.question: How is white displayed in RGB?
exercises.answer: Red, Green, and Blue all at maximum brightness
exercises.explain: When all three colors are at full brightness (255, 255, 255), they mix together to create white light.
choices: All channels are at half brightness (128)
Red, Green, and Blue all at maximum brightness
A special white channel is used
Only red is displayed at maximum

exercises.question: What color is displayed when all RGB channels are at 0?
exercises.answer: Black
exercises.explain: When red, green, and blue are all off (0, 0, 0), no light is produced. The pixel appears black.

exercises.question: What is color depth?
exercises.answer: The number of bits used per pixel to store color information
exercises.explain: Color depth determines how many colors can be displayed. A display using 8 bits per pixel shows only 256 colors, far fewer than the over 16 million of 24 bits per pixel.
choices: The brightness level of a color
The number of bits used per pixel to store color information

exercises.question: How many colors can a 24-bit display show?
exercises.answer: Over 16 million colors
exercises.explain: 24-bit color uses 8 bits per channel (RGB). Since each channel has 256 values, the total is 256 x 256 x 256 = 16,777,216 possible colors.

exercises.question: What is color gamut?
exercises.answer: The range of colors a display can actually produce
exercises.explain: Gamut describes which colors are possible on a specific screen. Not all displays can show the same colors, even with the same bit depth.
choices: The range of colors a display can actually produce

exercises.question: Why might two displays show the same image differently?
exercises.answer: They have different color gamuts and calibrations
exercises.explain: Each display has its own gamut, brightness range, and color balance. A photo might look warmer on one monitor and cooler on another.
choices: One uses more bits than the other
They have different color gamuts and calibrations

exercises.question: What is HDR in displays?
exercises.answer: High Dynamic Range, allowing brighter whites and darker blacks
exercises.explain: HDR displays can show a wider range of brightness, from very bright whites to very dark blacks, with more details in both extremes.
choices: High Dynamic Range, allowing brighter whites and darker blacks

units.title: Refresh Rate and Motion
units.tip: Refresh rate measures how many times per second the screen redraws the image. Response time measures how quickly pixels change color. Both affect motion smoothness.

exercises.question: What is refresh rate measured in?
exercises.answer: Hertz (Hz), cycles per second
exercises.explain: Refresh rate is how many times per second the screen redraws. 60 Hz means the image refreshes 60 times per second.

exercises.question: What does a 60 Hz monitor refresh?
exercises.answer: The image 60 times per second
exercises.explain: A 60 Hz display updates the image 60 times each second. This provides smooth motion for most everyday tasks.

exercises.question: Why do gaming monitors often have 144 Hz or higher?
exercises.answer: Higher refresh rates show motion more smoothly
exercises.explain: More frames per second means motion looks smoother and each step between frames is smaller, which helps in fast-paced games. The difference between 60 Hz and 144 Hz is easy to notice.
choices: Higher refresh rates show motion more smoothly
Higher refresh rates use less power
Higher refresh rates improve color accuracy

exercises.question: Can you see the difference between 60 Hz and 120 Hz?
exercises.answer: Yes, especially during fast motion or scrolling
exercises.explain: Most people notice smoother motion at 120 Hz compared to 60 Hz. The difference becomes less noticeable beyond 120 Hz for most people.
choices: Only if you look very carefully
No, the human eye cannot tell the difference
Yes, especially during fast motion or scrolling

exercises.question: What happens if your graphics card cannot keep up with the monitor refresh rate?
exercises.answer: Some frames are displayed twice, or the image tears
exercises.explain: If the GPU finishes a frame after the monitor has already started redrawing, either frames are duplicated or the screen shows parts of different frames.
choices: The refresh rate has no effect
Some frames are displayed twice, or the image tears

exercises.question: What is response time in a display?
exercises.answer: How fast a pixel changes from one color to another
exercises.explain: Response time measures how quickly pixels react to new input. Measured in milliseconds, it affects how sharp moving objects appear.
choices: How long data takes to reach the pixel
How bright the screen can get
How fast a pixel changes from one color to another

exercises.question: Why do gaming monitors advertise low response times?
exercises.answer: Slow response time causes blur during motion
exercises.explain: When pixels are slow to change, moving objects appear blurry. Low response times keep movement sharp and clear.
choices: Response time does not affect gaming
Low response time causes blur during motion
Low response time makes the image brighter
Slow response time causes blur during motion

exercises.question: What is ghosting in displays?
exercises.answer: A blurry shadow or trail following moving objects
exercises.explain: Ghosting occurs when pixels are slow to respond. You see a faint copy of the object trailing behind its actual position.
choices: Dead pixels that don't light up
A blurry shadow or trail following moving objects

exercises.question: What is screen tearing?
exercises.answer: Horizontal lines where the screen shows two different frames at once
exercises.explain: Tearing happens when the monitor shows part of one frame and part of the next. It creates a visible line where they don't match up.
choices: A permanent crack in the screen
Horizontal lines where the screen shows two different frames at once

exercises.question: What does VSync do?
exercises.answer: Synchronizes the GPU with the monitor refresh rate to prevent tearing
exercises.explain: VSync forces the GPU to wait for the monitor's refresh. This prevents tearing but can add input delay.
choices: Synchronizes the GPU with the monitor refresh rate to prevent tearing

units.title: Touchscreens and Input Devices
units.tip: Touchscreens detect where you touch them using different technologies. Keyboards and mice send input signals. Each input method has different accuracy and responsiveness.

exercises.question: What is a capacitive touchscreen?
exercises.answer: A screen that detects touch by sensing electrical conductivity
exercises.explain: Capacitive screens detect when your finger changes the electrical properties of the screen surface. They are sensitive and work with bare fingers.
choices: A screen that uses light reflection
A screen that uses heat to detect touch
A screen that detects touch by sensing electrical conductivity
A screen that uses pressure sensing

exercises.question: Why do capacitive touchscreens not work with gloves?
exercises.answer: Gloves block the electrical connection between your finger and the screen
exercises.explain: Most gloves are insulators, so they prevent the electrical signal from reaching the screen. Special conductive gloves are needed.
choices: The screen cannot see through gloves
Gloves block the electrical connection between your finger and the screen

exercises.question: What is a resistive touchscreen?
exercises.answer: A screen that detects touch by pressure between two conductive layers
exercises.explain: Resistive screens have two layers that come together when you press. They work with any object, including gloved fingers or styluses.
choices: A screen that only works with special pens
A screen that detects touch by pressure between two conductive layers
A screen that resists your touches
A screen that detects touch with infrared beams

exercises.question: What is a disadvantage of resistive touchscreens?
exercises.answer: They are less accurate and require more pressure than capacitive
exercises.explain: Resistive screens need visible pressure to register a touch. This makes them less responsive and less precise than capacitive screens.
choices: They are less accurate and require more pressure than capacitive
They do not work with fingers

exercises.question: What is multi-touch on a screen?
exercises.answer: The ability to detect multiple finger touches at the same time
exercises.explain: Multi-touch allows pinch-to-zoom, two-finger scrolling, and other gestures. Capacitive screens naturally support multi-touch.
choices: Touching the screen multiple times in a row
The ability to detect multiple finger touches at the same time
Touching different parts of the screen rapidly

exercises.question: What is the difference between membrane and mechanical keyboards?
exercises.answer: Mechanical has individual switches under each key; membrane uses a rubber sheet
exercises.explain: Mechanical keyboards have tactile switches that provide feedback. Membrane keyboards use a rubber dome under a single sheet, feeling mushy.
choices: Mechanical has individual switches under each key; membrane uses a rubber sheet

exercises.question: Why do gamers prefer mechanical keyboards?
exercises.answer: Tactile feedback and faster actuation improve response
exercises.explain: Mechanical switches give clear physical feedback when a key registers, and many have short travel before activating, which gamers value for control and timing.
choices: Tactile feedback and faster actuation improve response

exercises.question: What does a mouse sensor detect?
exercises.answer: Movement across a surface
exercises.explain: Mouse sensors track how far the mouse has moved. Different sensor types (optical, laser) use different methods but all measure movement.

exercises.question: What is DPI in mouse settings?
exercises.answer: Dots Per Inch, how much the cursor moves per mouse movement
exercises.explain: DPI controls sensitivity. High DPI makes the cursor move far when you move the mouse slightly. Low DPI requires more movement.
choices: Dots Per Inch, how much the cursor moves per mouse movement

exercises.question: How does a laser mouse typically differ from an optical mouse?
exercises.answer: Laser mice are more sensitive and work on more surfaces
exercises.explain: Laser sensors read finer surface detail, so they can track on glossy surfaces such as glass, where many optical sensors struggle.
choices: Laser mice are more sensitive and work on more surfaces
Optical mice do not use any light
Laser mice do not need electricity

units.title: Connectors and Ports
units.tip: Connectors are the physical plugs that attach devices to computers. Different connectors carry different types of data and power. Modern standards aim for faster speeds and reversibility.

exercises.question: What does HDMI stand for?
exercises.answer: High-Definition Multimedia Interface
exercises.explain: HDMI is a standard connector that carries video and audio together over one cable. It is the most common display connector.

exercises.question: What is DisplayPort?
exercises.answer: A digital display standard used mainly on computer monitors to carry video and audio
exercises.explain: DisplayPort was designed with computers in mind and supports high resolutions and refresh rates. It competes with HDMI.
choices: A digital display standard used mainly on computer monitors to carry video and audio

exercises.question: Can DisplayPort and HDMI be used on the same monitor?
exercises.answer: Yes, monitors often have both connectors
exercises.explain: Most modern monitors include both HDMI and DisplayPort inputs. You pick whichever one your computer supports.
choices: Yes, monitors often have both connectors
You must choose one when buying
No, a monitor uses only one

exercises.question: What is USB-C video output?
exercises.answer: USB-C ports that can transmit video signals as well as power and data
exercises.explain: USB-C is becoming a universal connector. Some USB-C ports support video output, allowing one cable to handle video and power.
choices: USB-C ports that can transmit video signals as well as power and data

exercises.question: Why is USB-C becoming popular for displays?
exercises.answer: It carries power, data, and video in one reversible connector
exercises.explain: USB-C simplifies device connections by combining multiple functions in one universal standard. The plug works either way up.
choices: It is only for mobile devices
It carries power, data, and video in one reversible connector
It has no limit on cable length

exercises.question: What does USB stand for?
exercises.answer: Universal Serial Bus
exercises.explain: USB is the standard for connecting peripherals to computers. It handles both data transfer and power delivery.

exercises.question: What is the main difference between USB 2.0 and USB 3.0?
exercises.answer: USB 3.0 is much faster
exercises.explain: USB 3.0 moves data many times faster than USB 2.0. Later USB versions are faster still.

exercises.question: Why is USB-C called reversible?
exercises.answer: The connector works when inserted either direction
exercises.explain: USB-C can be plugged in upside down or right-side up. Older USB-A connectors only worked one way.
choices: The connector works when inserted either direction

exercises.question: What is Thunderbolt?
exercises.answer: A high-speed data standard that works over USB-C connectors
exercises.explain: Thunderbolt is a very fast data link that uses the USB-C connector shape. Speeds have risen with each version.
choices: A high-speed data standard that works over USB-C connectors

exercises.question: Why do USB ports need different standards?
exercises.answer: Different devices need different speeds and power levels
exercises.explain: A keyboard needs little power and slow speeds, while an external hard drive needs fast speeds. USB standards give flexibility for these variations.
choices: There is no reason, it is just tradition
Manufacturers want to sell more cables
Older devices are incompatible with new standards
Different devices need different speeds and power levels
